instructions: Choose source references for one traveler answer from the COMPLETE indexed decision packet. Return only JSON choices, no prose or copied source facts. Use each source role exactly. The choices array has a strict maximum of eight references TOTAL, including any cash benchmark; that is a ceiling, not a target to fill. Use no duplicate references and at most one b. Choose a small useful set and a direct cash benchmark when available. When complete journeys exist, include a partial lead only if it adds distinct decision value; usually none is needed. With no complete journey, choose 2–3 relevant leads plus cash context when available. Select defensibly from route, timing, reported cabin scope, traveler and seat evidence, fare scope, costs and caveats. Points across programs are not comparable economic costs. The selected choices will receive exact source facts before writing. Ranking highlights in the packet are a starting point for a traveler answer, not a required or exhaustive selection. Choose the exact eligible journey that offers the clearest supported reason to take the next step, then add an alternative only when it changes a material decision dimension: route or schedule, reported cabin, program, known cash component, or limitation. Several near-identical variants, including a few minutes of timing, do not by themselves create useful alternatives. One journey is enough if the others add no material value. Do not fill a quota. Consider each option's own downside and the supported tradeoff; preserve conditional status, unknown totals and separate-ticket risk. Select an incomplete lead only when it changes the next useful action. The composer will see your selected facts, not the other eligible records, so choose deliberately.
